needs_human.note: A move now treats `Übung` and `übung` as one tag, while replace_file_tags and merge_file_tags on a drive treat them as different when the existing row holds the capital. The same two names merge or stay apart depending on the path that handled them.; Python str.lower() also folds compatibility characters such as U+212A KELVIN SIGN to `k`, so such a tag name would merge into an ASCII row on the destination.; When a file holds two case variants and the destination has neither, the surviving spelling depends on the order of File.tags, which the relationship does not define (backend/app/models.py:115-117).; `{src_drive} |` at backend/app/services/tagops.py:54 makes a move of a file that has only stale links also sweep unrelated orphan rows on the source drive, where the file left nothing.

No spec text or test states whether a moved tag should prefer an exact-name row on the destination over an older case variant; test_a_destination_holding_two_variants_resolves_to_the_older_row covers only a destination with no exact row.; Moving a non-ASCII lowercase tag onto a capitalised row merges two spellings that tag editing and the tag filter treat as separate tags.

A move merges non-ASCII case variants, while `replace_file_tags`, `merge_file_tags` and the tag filter keep them distinct. The tests pin this merge under an `UNSPEC` comment, so a person should confirm it.; When a legacy link is present, the move sweeps orphan rows on a third drive that is neither source nor destination, and that drive may be locked for the requester. Only rows with no linked file are deleted and nothing is returned, so no data is exposed, but the transaction writes outside the two drives named in the request.; The `files.moved` event names only the source and destination drives (`files.py:1438`, `files.py:422`), so an open tab on a swept third drive is not told its tag list changed.; A `.md` file moved onto a row with a different ASCII spelling keeps its frontmatter spelling, and a later projection renames the destination row for every file on that drive (`files.py:169-172`). This is unchanged from r1.
